fomo.item1: {bold} The official page says it returns in the Second Hunt for Astronomy, and tokens from this hunt carry over. Teamcraft's data also shows a second-hunt listing that sells tokens for 30 Astronomy II tomes, so missing a minimog week isn't fatal (datamined, could change).
fomo.item2Bold: MGP card, both special maps and the job mastery prisms are trove regulars.
fomo.item2: {bold} They're also stocked in the “previous” and “past” irregular tomestone exchanges, so there's no rush.
fomo.item3: {bold} the uolon horn (until the Second Hunt) and the Mameshiba Neckerchief. Everything else, including the Ananta and Kotokaze cards, has a permanent Triple Triad or NPC source.
fomo.item4: {bold} Dhalmel whistles and emerald bardings are already listing well under their recent median. If you're buying to sell, sell early.

cp.h1: Currency planner: what to buy before Evercold
cp.lede: Pick a currency you have piling up and see what it buys: the items that sell best on the market board right now, what's worth keeping for your collection, and whether to spend it before 8.0 or hold on to it.
cp.sellNote: Tradeable items ranked by gil per currency spent, using the average sale price on your market. Items selling less than once a day are marked slow: one big batch of those can sit unsold for weeks.
cp.collectNote: Mounts, minions, orchestrion rolls, cards and other unlocks this currency buys. When one also sells on the market board, the board price is shown so you can tell whether it is cheaper to buy it outright.
cp.sourcesShops: Which vendors exist and what each trade costs comes from {teamcraft}'s extracted shop data, which only counts vendors you can actually reach in game. Trades that also need a token or a second currency (most gear upgrades) are left out.
cp.sourcesItems: Item names in all four languages, icons and categories come from {xivapi}. Market prices and sales speed are pulled live from {universalis} for the market you pick.
cp.sourcesVerdict: The spend-or-keep notes are my read based on past expansion launches, not announced 8.0 changes. I will update them when the Evercold patch notes are out.
cp.priceFail: Some prices could not be loaded from Universalis. Try again in a minute.

verdictText.spend: Expected to lose most of its value at launch, based on past expansions.
verdictText.watch: Past expansions changed this kind of currency at launch, so don't stockpile it.
verdictText.keep: No change expected at launch. Spend it whenever it suits you.

notes.mnemonics: This tomestone only buys current endgame gear, and Evercold's first dungeons will replace that gear while you level. Buy only what you will use before launch. Past expansions retired the current tomestones in later patches.
notes.mathematics: Its gear will be outclassed at launch too, but Mathematics also buys raid-tier crafting materials that sell on the market board. Turning the spare ones into gil before 8.0 is the usual play.
notes.poetics: Poetics carry over between expansions, but you can hold at most 2,000. If you are near the cap, spend some on materials or collectibles so new ones are not wasted.
notes.orange-crafters: Past expansions added a new scrip tier at launch, and level 100 scrip gear will be outclassed. Materia and materials keep their value longer than gear.
notes.orange-gatherers: Past expansions added a new scrip tier at launch, and level 100 scrip gear will be outclassed. Materia and materials keep their value longer than gear.

cg.lede: Pick a job and see the cheapest HQ market board listing for every piece of its current crafted gear, live from Universalis: Courtly Lover for combat jobs, and Crested armor with Gold Thumb's tools for crafters and gatherers. Each job's full set total shows on its button, so you can see which ones are cheap to gear right now.
cg.priceFail: Could not reach Universalis. Try Refresh in a moment.
cg.dataFail: Could not load the gear list. Reload the page to try again.

notes.worlds: Prices are the lowest single listing on any world in the market you pick, so a full set usually means a few world visits. The 5% market tax is on top.
notes.hq: Prices are for HQ only. HQ and NQ share the same item level, but HQ adds roughly 10% more main stat plus extra substats, and nearly everything crafters list is HQ anyway, so NQ is rarely cheaper. Melding materia is up to you; listings that already have materia are counted too, if they happen to be cheapest.
notes.rings: Rings are not unique, so the two ring slots use the two cheapest ring listings.
notes.ornate: The combat body piece also comes as an "Ornate" version. It has the same base stats but five guaranteed materia slots instead of two, so you can meld it fully without risking overmelds. It is not crafted (earlier sets' Ornate pieces came from Wondrous Tails), so it is rare and usually costs far more. The page checks both and shows whichever is cheaper.
notes.shared: Jobs that wear the same armor set only need a new weapon: tanks share Fending, healers share Healing, magical ranged share Casting, and physical ranged share Aiming. Melee splits three ways: Maiming for Dragoon and Reaper, Striking for Monk and Samurai, and Scouting for Ninja and Viper. Accessories are shared more widely: Slaying covers Monk, Dragoon, Samurai, and Reaper, and Aiming covers physical ranged plus Ninja and Viper.
notes.crafting: Crafters and gatherers have no tradeable gear at the newest item level, so their list uses the best crafted gear you can buy: the item level 750 Crested set and Gold Thumb's tools. Every crafter wears the same Crested armor and every gatherer another, so a second crafter or gatherer only needs new tools.

cg.sourcesItems: Item list, item and job names in all four languages, and icons come from {xivapi}, saved as crafted-gear.json and refreshed when a new crafted set comes out.
cg.sourcesPrices: Market prices are pulled live from the {universalis} API each time you load the page or press Refresh. Universalis only knows what players with its uploader have seen, so a listing can be gone by the time you get there. The time under each price says when that item's data was last updated.

housingForBeginners.title: FFXIV Housing for Beginners: Permits, Limits, and First Steps | XIVKit
housingForBeginners.description: A beginner's guide to FFXIV housing: the order to do things in, how permits and ownership work, furnishing limits by size, sharing with friends, upkeep, cheap furnishing, and useful tools.

craftedGear.title: FFXIV Crafted Gear Prices: Courtly Lover Set by Job | XIVKit
craftedGear.description: Pick a job and see the cheapest HQ market board price for every piece of its crafted gear, live from Universalis: the item level 770 Courtly Lover set for combat jobs, and Crested gear with Gold Thumb's tools for crafters and gatherers, laid out like the in-game Character window.

index.title: XIVKit: FFXIV Tools & Links
index.description: Curated FFXIV tools and links, marked by whether I use them or haven't tried them yet: theorycrafting calculators, market board data, crafting trackers, and reference sites.

plugins.title: FFXIV Plugins | XIVKit
plugins.description: Dalamud plugins I actually use for FFXIV: client-side tools, some from the default plugin directory, some added as custom/experimental repos.

huntForAstronomy.title: FFXIV Hunt for Astronomy Rewards: Worth the Tomes? | XIVKit
huntForAstronomy.description: Every reward in FFXIV's Hunt for Astronomy trove, where else it drops, what it sells for on the market board, and a straight verdict on whether it's worth the tomestones. Filterable, with a running tomestone budget tracker.

msqTracker.title: FFXIV MSQ Tracker with a Shareable Link | XIVKit
msqTracker.description: Track your FFXIV Main Scenario Quest progress from A Realm Reborn through Dawntrail. Your current quest lives in the page link so you can paste it to friends, and you can export a PNG progress card.

currencyPlanner.title: FFXIV Currency Planner: What to Buy Before Evercold | XIVKit
currencyPlanner.description: Pick an FFXIV currency (tomestones, scrips, bicolor gemstones, seals, MGP and more) and see what to buy with it before Evercold: the best items for gil with live market prices, what's worth collecting, and whether to spend it before 8.0.

hh.s40: Once you are in, {t1} cover decorating, and {t2} covers letting friends use it.
hh.s44: There is no single start-here guide that covers both the outside and the inside of a house, and no official beginner guide on the Lodestone. The best pair is the wiki for rules and the HGXIV guide for decorating.
hh.s59: There is only one housing permit.
hh.s68: A character can hold one personal house and, if they lead an FC, one FC house, plus one apartment. Personal and FC plots cannot be converted into each other. The wiki words the one-house rule two different ways, so confirm in game.
hh.s69: Land is sold by lottery on a 9-day cycle (5 days of entry, 4 of results), one entry per period. A small plot costs 3,000,000 to 3,750,000 gil depending on plot grade. Price does not change by district. The full price is held as a deposit while you wait. Losing entries are refunded in full, and a winner who does not finalize the purchase forfeits 50% of the deposit.
hh.s70: {t1} hiring a vendor for your house also uses "permits". The cheapest is the 3,000 gil Steward Permit for an Estate Manservant or Maidservant.
hh.s73: The owner of a personal house can make up to {t1} "tenants". Tenants can teleport to the house and, if you allow it, decorate and garden. The game calls this Estate Sharing. There is no cost.
hh.s76: {t1} They must be from your home world.
hh.s77: Add them to your Friend List first.
hh.s78: Open the {t1} menu (in the Social menu), then go to {t2}, pick your estate, and choose {t3}. That page can take a minute to load, so wait for it.
hh.s82: Pick your friend from the list and add them as a tenant.

hh.s254: Anyone who has friends or an FC visiting, or a house on a public tour.
hh.s257: Grows one crop indoors. It is the only way to grow flower seeds, and the only way to garden in an apartment. Flower seeds cost 300 gil from Material Suppliers and Apartment Merchants. See the Flowerpots section above for counts.
hh.s258: Housing Merchants in all five districts, and the Apartment Merchant in apartment lobbies. Comes in Riviera, Glade, and Oasis styles.
hh.s260: Indoors, as a tabletop piece. Put it on a shelf or table where you will see it, and visit once an hour to tend it.

hh.s266: Round 3,000 gil (4 beds), Oblong 12,000 gil (6 beds), Deluxe 48,000 gil (8 beds and a scarecrow)
hh.s267: Outdoors, in the yard. A small house has one patch, so the 8-bed Deluxe gets the most from it. Plant, fertilize once an hour, and tend.

hh.s269: Small 1, Medium 2, Large 3. None for apartments.
hh.s271: Housing vendors are hired with a permit bought from an Independent Sutler in each residential district, or an Apartment Merchant in apartment lobbies. They share one limit across all types: 4 in an apartment, {t1}, 8 in a medium, 10 in a large. Pick the ones you will really use. A Mender and a Steward are the usual first two.
hh.s277: Repairs your gear for gil (to 100% only).

hh.s286: Melds materia for gil. Cannot overmeld.

A small house holds {t1} facilities, so choose the classes you are leveling. They are crafted or bought on the Market Board, with no vendor price. Owners and tenants can use them in a personal house, and any member in an FC house. The wiki lists the CP bonus as +10, which we have not tested.

hh.s316: If a house is demolished, you can recover 80% of the plot price from the caretaker within 35 days. Permits and exteriors are not refunded.
hh.s318: Housing Merchants sell the basics for little. Walls, floors, rugs, and bookshelves run about 5,000 gil, chairs and tables about 2,000, and lamps 3,000 to 4,000. Furnishing a small house from merchants alone is plausibly well under 1,000,000 gil (our estimate, not a sourced figure).

hh.s339: These are in Dalamud's default plugin directory, so no custom repo is needed. Search the plugin's name in the in-game installer to find it. Third-party plugins are client mods and are not endorsed by Square Enix. Use them at your own risk.
hh.s350: Other default-repo housing helpers: Housing Herald, Facade, Doorbell, Allagan Tools, Item Search, and Price Insight. BDTH, which lets players go past normal placement limits, is not in the default repo and would need a custom repo, so we are not recommending it here. Better Housing is listed but looks abandoned (last updated December 2023). More on our {t1}.
hh.s353: Evercold releases February 23, 2027, with early access on February 19. Secondary sources report that Yoshida confirmed two housing overhauls for that window: a UI overhaul aimed at casual players, and a second one he did not name. Anything beyond that, including new plots, is speculation, so do not plan around it. See our {t1}.

hh.s365: Just got a cottage (or dreaming of one)? Here's the order to do things in, the rules that trip people up, cheap ways to furnish, and the tools worth knowing. Tell us what you've got and the page tailors itself.
hh.s372: Numbers come from community wikis and third-party articles, not official patch notes, so confirm them in game.
hh.s384: The order most people follow, start to finish. Tick them off as you go, and this page will remember.
hh.s387: A personal house needs a level 50 combat class and Second Lieutenant rank in a Grand Company. An apartment is the cheap way in while you save up. See {t1}.
hh.s389: A small plot is 3,000,000 to 3,750,000 gil, and the full price is held as a deposit while you wait. Then the Construction Permit is another 450,000 gil, plus furniture.
hh.s391: You get one entry per 9-day cycle (5 days of entry, 4 of results). If you do not win, the deposit is refunded in full (the wiki says within 90 days). If you win and do not finalize, you lose 50% of it.
hh.s393: After you win, buy the size-matched Construction Permit at the Estate Hall. You have 45 days to build or the land is reclaimed. Pick the four required exterior pieces: roof, wall, windows, and door.
hh.s395: Housing Merchants sell the basics for a few thousand gil, and you can preview their items before you buy. See {t1}.
hh.s397: A small house holds 300 indoor and 40 yard furnishings. See {t1}.
hh.s399: Go in at least once every 45 days, or the house is demolished. See {t1}.
hh.s401: The "Personal Estate Permit" and "Free Company Estate Permit" do not exist as separate items. After you win a plot, buy the size-matched {t1} at the Estate Hall, then build within 45 days.
hh.s407: Needs a level 50 combat class and Second Lieutenant rank in a Grand Company. Can be shared with up to 3 friends (see {t1}).
hh.s409: Needs FC rank 6, at least 4 members, and 30 days of membership for the buyer. Only FC houses have Private Chambers (300,000 gil each).
hh.s410: One per character, 500,000 gil, and it sits outside the house limit. Not subject to demolition. No yard or garden.
hh.s412: 300,000 gil for your own room inside your FC's house. Same space and limits as an apartment. Needs level 50 and Second Lieutenant rank. Not refunded if the house is demolished.
hh.s419: Bars are relative to a Large mansion. Private Chambers and apartments share the same limits.
hh.s436: A small house gets one patch, so only the Deluxe fills the 8-bed allowance.
